MFA No. 201794 of 2016 (BY SRI UDAY P. HONGUNTIKAR, ADVOCATE FOR R2;
 V/O DATED 10.07.2023 BRINGING LRS OF R1 IS DISPENSED  WITH)

THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988 PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26/11/2015 PASSED BY THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER MACT-IX AT BASAVANA BAGEWADI IN MVC NO.64/2011, BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimants have filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT - IX, Basavana Bagewadi (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.64/2011 vide its judgment and award dated 26.11.2015.

2. The claimants are the parents and sisters of the deceased - Umar Farookh, who died in a road traffic accident on 27.11.2010 when a lorry bearing registration No.MH-10/A- 6009 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle') dashed against him while he was walking by the side of the road and ran over him.
As a result, he suffered injuries and was declared brought dead at the hospital.
The claimants claimed that the deceased was 20 years old and was a mason, earning a sum of Rs.4,500 per month and that they were deprived of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5517 his financial and emotional support.
Hence, they filed a claim petition claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer of the offending vehicle who denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimants for the compensation.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and Exs.p1 to P5 were marked.
An eyewitness was examined as PW.2

The insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked Ex.R1.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

It held that the deceased was 20 years old and his income was considered at a sum of Rs.4,000/- per month of which 50% was deducted towards his personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation was awarded:-

2 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5517 Sl. Particulars Amount No. (in Rs.) 1 For transportation of the dead 20,000/-
body and funeral expenses 2 For loss of estate 25,000/- 3 Love and affection 20,000/- 4 For loss of dependency 4,32,000/-
(Rs.48,000/- x  x 18) Total 4,97,000/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants have filed this appeal.
7.
The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.5,500/- as is done in similar cases.
He also contended that the deceased was 20 years old and therefore, 40% of the loss of future prospects must have been factored.

The learned counsel for the insurer does not dispute the above fact but contends that the claimants themselves claimed that the income of the deceased was Rs.4,500/- per month and submits that the notional income cannot be applied in this case.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.

10. The fact that the deceased was a 20 year old able bodied man and was employed as a mason,
makes it more than probable that his income could not be less than Rs.5,000/- per month.
Thus, it is appropriate to consider the notional income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month.
The claimants were entitled to loss of future prospects at the rate of 40% of Rs.5,000/-.
Since the deceased was a bachelor 50% of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

11. Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-

Sl. Particulars Amount No. (in Rs.) 1

Towards loss of dependency 7,56,000/-
(5,000 + 40% x 12 x 18 x ) 2 Towards loss of filial consortium 40,000/- 3

Towards loss of estate, funeral 30,000/-

sentences.text: Since the liability of the insurer is not challenged, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
13. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.4,97,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.8,26,000/-.
The enhanced compensation is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
However, the claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 261 days in filing the appeal.

14. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant No.1 in any nationalized Bank for a period of five years.
